terms.meaning: a reusable piece of the screen written as a function that returns the markup to show
a value a parent passes into a component
an extra tag setting, such as data-state, that style rules can match
text that screen readers speak in place of visual content

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Allowed data state type
sections.what: Brings in the list of allowed data states from the domain types file, so the badge only accepts valid states.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the state names in one shared place.

sections.name: DataStateBadge
sections.title: Badge showing the data state
sections.what: Shows the label inside a status badge tagged with its state, so the colour matches that state. It is marked as a status region for screen readers and labelled with the word Data.
sections.why: Likely reason: every data panel needs a visible and spoken data status.
sections.watch_out: Because it is a status region, screen readers may announce each change, so frequent label updates could be noisy.

summary: A small status label that tells the user what kind of data a panel shows, such as live, stale or historical replay.
purpose: Makes data freshness visible on every data panel so that no panel can look live when it is not.
why: The comment above the component says every data panel must say what kind of data it shows.
how: Takes a state and a label. Shows the label as text in a badge. Sets the state as a data attribute, which the stylesheet uses for colour. Sets an accessible label that starts with the word Data.
inputs: state (a DataState value from the sources types file) and label (the text to show).
outputs: A badge element on screen. Nothing is stored.
risks: The label is shown exactly as given, so a wrong label misleads the user. A state with no matching style rule appears with default colour.
debug: If the colour is wrong, compare the state value with the rules in components.css. If the text is wrong, check the label the parent panel passes in.
